title: Compute-path profiler and conditional executor for mixed-seqlen workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Large variance in request sequence lengths and mixed-architecture fleet (A100, H100, RTX) leads to frequent suboptimal kernel choices at runtime. Current heuristics use coarse seqlen buckets and static per-arch defaults which cause tail latency spikes and unnecessary cost from pessimistic fallbacks.

Goal:
Deliver a lightweight compute-path profiler and a conditional executor that uses per-request microprofiles plus an online warmstart cache to pick the best kernel implementation and operator layout for given (arch, batch, seqlen, token-phase) inputs with negligible added latency. Reduce 99th latency by 10-20% for mixed workloads and decrease per-token cost for mid-length requests (64-512) by ~5%.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Runtime microprofiler: run very short latency probes (prefill/first decode step) on cold paths or when seqlen/arch combination is unseen. Probes are lightweight synthetic microbenchmarks using the same device context and a representative token window.
- Conditional executor: policy layer that decides between immediate execution, use cached kernel, or run probe then execute. Policy evaluates predicted tail risk vs probe overhead.
- Per-arch warmstart cache: fingerprint (arch, model-shape-hash, batch, seqlen-histogram, quantized-flag) -> best kernel id + confidence + recent metrics. Eviction by LRU+staleness.
- Continuous online calibration: collect decode latency, occupancy, and KV-cache hit stats. Use low-cost aggregated telemetry to decay confidence and trigger re-probing on distribution shifts.
- Offline microbenchmark harness: nightly hunts that validate probe results against extended microbench runs and update kernel candidates for an arch/model combo.

Acceptance criteria:
- Feature toggled and gateable per-customer in runtime config.
- End-to-end added median latency overhead from profiler <= 0.5ms for eligible requests; p99 improvement >= 10% on mixed seqlen trace in canary region.
- Telemetry dashboard with: per-fingerprint latency distribution, probe hit/miss rate, probe overhead distribution, kernel selection accuracy vs offline ground truth.
- Safety rollback: if probe-derived selections cause regressions > 5% p99 increase for 24h, auto-disable for that fingerprint.

Telemetry & metrics to collect:
- probe_count, probe_success, probe_latency_ms, kernel_selection_id, selection_confidence, post_exec_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit, occupancy_pct, resumed_from_warmstart, staleness_seconds.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature branch: implement profiler + cache + policy behind flag, unit tests + microbench harness.
2) Canary region (us-west-2) for low-traffic models with dedicated canary pool. 2 weeks run.
3) Expand to mixed-arch dedicated clusters (1% traffic). Monitor telemetry; run offline validator nightly.
4) Gradual ramp by model tier + customer opt-in; default off for high-SLA customers until validated.

Risks & mitigation:
- Probe overhead adds latency: keep probe only on cold fingerprints and amortize via warmstart cache. Cap probes per node per minute.
- Incorrect probe measurements (noise): use median-of-3 microprobe strategy and confidence threshold.
- Security/customer data exposure: probes use synthetic tokens and never log customer prompt content.

Implementation notes & questions for design review:
- Microprobe implementation should reuse existing prefill scheduling path to avoid duplicating tensor setup; can we instrument prefill to run a "dry-run" profiler?
- Cache fingerprint: what fields give best discriminative power without explosion (suggested: model-shape-hash, seqlen_bucket, batch, device_compute_capability, quantization_scheme, kv_cache_enabled).
- Policy thresholds should be configurable via runtime knobs and remote-config UI in Console.

Artifacts & links:
- Design spec (internal): https://confluence.company/realtime/computepath-profiler (draft)
- Microbench harness repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt-microbench/pull/214
- Canary dashboard (grafana): https://grafana.company/d/rt/profiler-canary
- Initial perf notebook with traces: https://drive.company/drive/folders/rt/profiler-notebooks/seed-trace-analysis.ipynb

Next steps:
- Prototype microprobe (Marco) + hook into runtime prefill path (Aisha).
- Create telemetry schema and kafka topic (infra) for probe events.
- Draft console config and feature flag controls (PM/design).
comments: 2026-01-14 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes added. We agreed microprobe should be synthetic and not touch any customer tokens. Action: Marco to spike a single-step prefill probe (2d).

2026-01-19 - Marco Liu: Spike complete. Microprobe reuses allocator and warms kernel cache; median probe latency on A100 is 0.4ms (single-step). Pushed initial code to feature/profiler-spike branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt-runtime/compare/feature/profiler-spike
2026-01-22 - Eng Review: Reviewed probe noise. We saw 18% variance during noisy co-tenancy on shared nodes. Decision: use median-of-N samples and require confidence > 0.7 to cache result.

2026-02-02 - QA: Integration tests added for probe fallback and cache eviction (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt-runtime/pull/882). Observed a transient p99 regression in nightly 3hr test due to aggressive probe frequency; lowered probe cap from 20->5 per node per minute.

2026-02-18 - Data: Offline validator nightly job shows 95% agreement between microprobe choice and full microbench on A100/H100 for seqlen 32/128/512. Disagreements concentrated on quantized kernels for seqlen=512.

2026-03-05 - PM (Leah Kim): Please confirm whether customer-facing knob is "profiler: on/off" or fine-grained per-model controls. Decided: provide both — global and per-model flags in Console (work to track in PM ticket).
2026-03-10 - Marco Liu: Preparing canary rollout plan. Canary pool provisioning requested to infra. Marking ready for canary once infra greenlights capacity.
